name: claim_enrichment_table_record
description:
Checks and marks a key in a `memory` enrichment table in one step, so a burst of events
with the same key counts every event even before the table publishes its writes to
readers.

A claim opens a window of `window_secs` when the key has no row inside a window: no
row at all, or one in its carry period, the time between the end of its window and the
end of its `ttl_secs`. The window stays fixed from then on. Each claim in the window
counts; the first `cap` of them pass. The returned object has `pass`, `first` (this
claim opened the window), `count` (this claim's position in the window, from 1),
`suppressed_prev` (on a claim that opens a window over a row in its carry period, how
many that row's window suppressed; otherwise 0), `window_secs` (the window in force)
and `value` (what the opening claim stored).

The row is written through the table's own write path, so its size cap, TTL scan and
persistence apply to it. A claim the size cap refuses is an error, not a pass.

arguments.name: table
arguments.description: The [enrichment table](/docs/reference/glossary/#enrichment-tables) to claim the key in. Only `memory` tables support claims.

arguments.name: key
arguments.description: The key to check and mark.

arguments.name: window_secs
arguments.description: The length of the window this claim opens, in seconds. At least 1. A claim opens a window when the key has no row inside one: no row at all, or one in its carry period. A window already open keeps its own length.

arguments.name: cap
arguments.description: How many claims in one window pass. At least 1.

arguments.name: ttl_secs
arguments.description: How long the row lives from the start of the window this claim opens, in seconds. At least `window_secs`, which is the default. The time past the window is the carry period: a claim in it opens a new window, with its own `window_secs` and `ttl_secs`, and reports how many the previous window suppressed.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: A value stored by the claim that opens the window and returned to every claim in it.

internal_failure_reasons: The table does not support claims.
The table is full and refused the row.

examples.title: Throttle a key to one event a minute
